Lemma 3 (Day 84): Assuming D1 (odd c) + (E) beta'(4k)=beta(4k), we have Delta beta'(4k+2) + Delta beta'(4k+4) = 9 + 2 v_2(k) for all k >= 1. Elementary proof via Kummer identity for Delta beta and case analysis on D1. Data-verified at k=1,2. Consequence: closes half of the even-c dip pattern.

(E): beta'(4k) = beta(4k) for all k >= 1. Empirical at k=1 (beta'(4)=4) and k=2 (beta'(8)=11). Structural rationale: at c=0 mod 4 the ambient Kummer floor and the heavy-quotient floor coincide because the internal 2-adic slack (opened at odd c=1 mod 8) closes back up at the next 4-boundary.

D2: for k >= 1, beta'(4k+2) = beta(4k+2) - 1 - v_2(k). Data-consistent at k=1 (D(6)=1) and k=2 (D(10)=2). Not implied by D1+(E) individually — only the sum Delta beta'(4k+2) + Delta beta'(4k+4) is forced. D2 is the natural interpolation of the data.

Theorem (Day 85, c = 5): M_j(a, b, 5) = sum over partitions mu of 2j (with at most 3 rows) of K_{mu^T, (2^j)} * f^{(a,b,5)/mu}, where K_{mu^T, (2^j)} = [s_mu : e_2^j] = coefficient of s_mu in e_2^j. Equivalent Hall-inner-product form: M_j = <s_lambda, e_2^j * p_1^{n-2j}>. Coefficient sums (1, 1, 2, 4, 9, 21) are Motzkin numbers.
